What Happens When You Call an LLM API

One POST /v1/chat/completions, followed through every layer it touches: gateway, load balancer, tokenizer, a hidden model router, the inference engine (prefill, decode, attention, GPUs), post-processing, billing and logging. Press ▶ Send a request to watch it travel, or open any layer to play with it.

0 ms
0 msInference is most of the wait—

"You type a prompt. ~400 ms and 14 infrastructure layers later, you get your answer."

Timings are the illustrative figures of the source picture (gateway ~5 ms, load balancer ~2 ms, tokenization ~3 ms, routing ~1 ms, inference ~300–800 ms, post-processing and response ~5 ms each); real numbers vary by provider, model, region and load. Tokenizer, attention and sampling demos are simplified models, labelled as such. Applies broadly to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Cohere, Mistral, AWS Bedrock and Azure AI. Layout adapted from a public infographic by Brij Kishore Pandey. Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site; Anthropic's API is one of the providers this describes.
